preamble: In Southern Bantu, the Proto-Bantu palatal consonant *c (and voiced *j) developed into the voiceless alveolar lateral fricative [ɬ], written hl. Van der Vlugt and Gunnink (2025) show that alveolar lateral obstruents reconstruct to Proto-Nguni as the regular reflex of Proto-Bantu *c and *j; the same outcome appears in Sotho, while Tswana has the lateral affricate tlh [tɬʰ]. The exact phonetic value of Proto-Bantu *c (palatal stop or affricate) is reconstructed, so the precise starting point is uncertain.

examples.note: Sesotho hl is [ɬ]; the closely related Tswana form leitlho has the lateral affricate [tɬʰ] instead.

sources: van der Vlugt, N., & Gunnink, H. (2025). Inheritance and Contact in the Development of Lateral Obstruents in Nguni Languages (S40). Languages, 10(5), 90. https://doi.org/10.3390/languages10050090
